beats.text: It came from one man memorising nonsense.
beats.note: Hermann Ebbinghaus was the only subject in his own experiments, reported in 1885.

beats.name: Hermann Ebbinghaus
beats.role: Learned lists of meaningless syllables, then measured how much effort it took to relearn them later.

beats.context: In each list of the 2015 replication, set out in rows of 13.

beats.note: At the University of Amsterdam, Joeri Dros, a 22 year old, was the only subject. It took about 70 hours.
It closely matched Ebbinghaus's data. Only the 31 day score came out much lower.
The authors saw a likely jump from the 24 hour point, which sleep research would predict. The paper does not prove sleep caused it.

beats.text: Two men, 130 years apart, one curve.

beats.line: The most cited memory graph began with a single volunteer.
